names.name: The night shift
names.said: The light is on and the door is locked, and that is the shop working.

text.what: The hours the work actually happens in: dough started in the small hours so the case is full when the door opens.
text.story:
Krispy Kreme's hot donut began as a by-product of exactly this. Vernon Rudolph's Winston-Salem shop sold wholesale to grocery stores, and production ran from midnight to four in the morning; he sold hot donuts to whoever turned up during it. The window came later; the schedule came first.

A raised dough sets the clock. It has to be mixed, risen, cut, proofed and fried before opening, and none of those steps can be hurried by much.
text.how: Mix around midnight or one. Raised first, cake after. Glaze, ice, fill, sprinkle, load the case, unlock the door.
text.today: The shift is the part of the business that does not scale, and the part a family absorbs. *Inference —* it is also the reason a second generation often does not take the shop on.

kin.as: The chain that sold the by-product.
Sold hot donuts to the people awake at 2 a.m.
